newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: NZ govt to stick to spending limits despite growth.
newsitem.headline: NZ govt to stick to spending limits despite growth.

text.p: New Zealand Deputy Prime Minister and Treasurer Winston Peters said on Monday his government would stick to agreed public spending limits despite recent figures showing strong economic growth in the last year.

"We made it clear we would stick to the expenditure that has been announced with one significant qualification, and that is that it is within fiscal limits. We intend to maintain expenditure within those fiscal limits," Peters told reporters.
Peters, leader of the New Zealand First party, which is part of a coalition government with the National Party, was speaking after a series of meetings with Singapore leaders.

The incoming New Zealand government agreed to boost public spending by NZ$5 billion over three years as part of the coalition pact after the elections last October. But Peters said this increase was a ceiling.

"That's a ceiling. That's on an all things being equal basis. Should there be some untoward event such as a hailstorm over three quarters of New Zealand and production drops away, we would have to take that into account," he said.
He said the latest figures gave him no more scope for public spending or for tax cuts, other than those already announced.
"There will be tax cuts on July 1, 1998. As to further tax cuts that will be contigent upon further economic growth," he said.
